correctness.rationale: For an invariant compactly supported measure, applying the generator to arbitrary functions of \(z\) gives \(\mathbb E[y^2-a\mid z]=0\). Applying it to arbitrary functions of \(Q\) and using \(LQ=-2az\) gives \(\mathbb E[z\mid Q]=0\) when \(a\ne0\). The exact identity \(L(zQ)=(y^2-a)Q-2az^2\) yields the covariance formula. The \(a<0\) obstruction and \(a=0\) classification follow from nonnegativity and \(L(xy)=y^2-x^2-xyz\). Strictness for \(a>0\) follows because an invariant compact support contained in \(z=0\) would force \(y^2=a\) along a complete trajectory, hence nonzero constant \(y\) and unbounded \(x\). The packaged exact-arithmetic checker verifies all polynomial generator identities.

value.rationale: The same-object literature centers on the transition from invariant spheres at \(a=0\) to hidden attractors, periodic orbits, and invariant tori when the first integral disappears. The final theorem gives a quantitative stationary remnant of that geometry: every compact recurrent component obeys a heightwise kinetic law, every radius shell has zero conditional thermostat mean, and the loss of radial conservation is measured exactly by a strictly positive covariance equal to radial derivative energy. Together with the complete \(a\le0\) compact-measure classification and forced excursions for \(a>0\), this is a structural global recurrence statement rather than a routine normalization check.
